Abortion has long been one of the most debated moral issues in society. To many people, abortion is viewed as wrong because it involves ending a developing human life and raises serious ethical questions about human dignity, responsibility, and the value of life itself. From this perspective, abortion is not just a medical procedure—it is a moral decision with lasting emotional, social, and ethical consequences.

A central argument against abortion is the belief that human life begins at conception. Even in its earliest form, the unborn child is seen as a unique human being with its own DNA, potential, and intrinsic worth. Ending that life is viewed as ending a human future: a future of growth, relationships, and experiences that the child will never have.
